presentation.label: TAPE SATURATION
presentation.summary: JClones TapeHead on the DSP: a small tape-style saturator with drive, trim and three tone colours.
presentation.overview: TapeHead runs the input through a two-state recursion whose corner frequency COLOR sets, drives both states into cubic smoothstep curves and adds a clipped feedback term. Low DRIVE gives gentle rounding and a slight tilt; high DRIVE flattens peaks and thickens the low end. It is a buffer-free insert, so it runs on FX1 or FX2 of every track.
highlights: Port of JClones_TapeHead.jsfx, within 4.7e-4 of the float reference in a native render
DRIVE and TRIM as continuous 0-127 knobs over the JSFX ranges
COLOR: NORM, MED and BRGT corners at 2100, 3680 and 5000 Hz
No buffers: FX1 or FX2 on any track, 288 cycles/sample static
usage: Assign TAPEHEAD in FUNC + FX2 (or FX1) SETUP with LEVEL and YES. Defaults match the JSFX: DRIVE 36, TRIM 18 (-3 dB), COLOR NORM.
Raise DRIVE for more saturation; lower TRIM (towards 0) to bring the level back up, raise it to attenuate down to -21 dB.
Use COLOR for brightness: MED and BRGT move the recursion's corner up and let more top end through the saturator.

controls.name: DRIVE
controls.doc: Tape drive. 0-127 maps to the JSFX drive 1-10 (gain 0.8x to 8x into the curves); 36 is about the JSFX default 3.5.

controls.name: TRIM
controls.doc: Output trim. 0 is 0 dB, 127 is -21 dB; 18 is the JSFX default -3 dB. Higher values are quieter.

controls.name: COLOR
controls.doc: Corner frequency of the recursion: NORM 2100 Hz, MED 3680 Hz, BRGT 5000 Hz.

limitations: The JSFX Clip switch is not exposed. Clip is always on (the JSFX default), because Q1.23 cannot carry the unclipped mode.
Corner frequencies assume 44.1 kHz, the rate every Octamod effect assumes.

presentation.label: MODULATED SPACE
presentation.summary: A modulated feedback-delay reverb after the Erbe-Verb: size, decay past 100 %, absorb, chorus, grains, shimmer, reverse and tilt.
presentation.overview: Four delay lines with diffusing allpasses, absorbing low-passes and a soft-saturating decay feed each other through a Hadamard matrix at 22.05 kHz. DPTH sweeps from a cyclic chorus through random ergodic grains into octave shimmer; REV plays the pre-delay backwards; EDCY and ESIZ route the reverb's own envelope into decay and size. The dry signal is never processed.
highlights: Size from a 2 ms box to a 143 ms hall, gliding without zipper noise
Decay up to 120 %: sustains and saturates above about 106
Cyclic, ergodic and shimmer modulation on one bipolar knob, with its speed beside it
Reverse pre-delay, tilt EQ and envelope-to-decay/size routings
MIX 0 is the exact dry signal
usage: Choose E-Verb in FX2 SETUP: hold FUNC, press FX2, turn LEVEL to the end of the list and press YES.

On the main page, MIX (encoder F) sets dry/wet; SIZE, DCY and ABSB shape the space; DPTH left is chorus, right is grains, the last sixteen steps are shimmer; SPD sets how fast it moves. Hold FUNC while turning a knob to jump between 0, the centre (64) and 127.
On the SETUP page, TILT darkens or brightens the wet, PRE sets the pre-delay, REV reverses it, and EDCY/ESIZ send the reverb's envelope into DCY and SIZE.
The six main-page knobs take parameter locks, LFOs, scenes and MIDI CC like any stock effect's; the SETUP knobs are set per Part.

controls.name: SIZE
controls.doc: Scales every delay and allpass over six octaves: the longest line runs 2.2 ms at 0, 18 ms at 64 and 143 ms at 127. Moving it glides the pitch of the tail, smoothed per frame.

controls.name: DCY
controls.doc: Reflection gain from 0 to 120 %. Below about 106 the tail decays (short at 40, minutes at 100 with large sizes); above, it sustains and the in-loop saturation holds the level.

controls.name: ABSB
controls.doc: 0..38 adds diffusion (allpass gain up to 0.8); 38..127 adds damping inside the loop, darker and shorter.

controls.name: DPTH
controls.doc: Bipolar modulation, 0 at the centre. Left: cyclic chorus/doppler. Right: ergodic grains to +47; from +48 a growing share of grains glides up an octave (shimmer), about half at +56.

controls.name: SPD
controls.doc: Modulation speed 0.5 Hz to 256 Hz (about 12 Hz at 64): the cyclic rate or the grain rate; in the shimmer zone SIZE sets the grain length.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Equal-power dry/wet. 0 is exactly the dry input; 127 is all reverb.

controls.name: TILT
controls.doc: SETUP A. Bipolar wet tone. Left: lows below 250 Hz up to +12 dB, highs down (about -14 dB at 9 kHz). Right: highs above 2 kHz up to +24 dB, lows down 3 to 5 dB. Centre is flat. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: PRE
controls.doc: SETUP B. Pre-delay 7 ms at 0, 42 ms at 64, 227 ms from 124 to 127 (up to 250 ms before 0.1.2); with REV on, the reverse window (at least 42 ms). Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: REV
controls.doc: SETUP C. Plays the pre-delay buffer backwards in crossfaded windows; a change ducks, switches in silence and reopens without a click. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: EDCY
controls.doc: SETUP D. Bipolar: the reverb's envelope into DCY. Left reins the tail in when loud; right rings longer when loud, up to the decay of DCY 95, never into sustain (no effect from DCY 96 up). Centre is off. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: ESIZ
controls.doc: SETUP E. Bipolar: the reverb's envelope into SIZE. Left shrinks the space when loud; right grows it. Centre is off. Not lockable (SETUP page).

limitations: 0.1.1 and 0.1.2 have not run on hardware. 0.1.1 changed only FUNC + turn on SIZE, DCY, ABSB and SPD (four descriptor bytes); 0.1.2 shortens the DSP ring to 15,870 words and caps the pre-delay at 227 ms from PRE 124 (issue #696), measured on the DSP emulator. The owner's MKII report (working sound, two distinct simultaneous T1/T5 instances, Part/project save and reload, physical reboot) is for 0.1.0 on EVRB01T01. MKI, maximum-load silicon timing and broader hardware modulation/recovery tests remain unverified.

FX2 only: the effect needs the 16K-word delay buffer the OS gives FX2 instances. It uses the first 15,870 words and leaves the last 514 (+$3DFE..+$3FFF) to Sidechain Compressor's cross-core key window on T3 and T7 (issue #696).

Projects saved with 0.1.1 store the same knob values and should sound the same unless PRE is 124 or higher; those settings now play 227 ms (they gave 230 to 250 ms). Reloading a 0.1.1 project into 0.1.2 is not tested.

With stock DSP code built in, E-Verb's 1,602 words take the space of two FX2-only stock reverbs. presentation.label: BUCKET BRIGADE
presentation.summary: A bucket-brigade delay: compander, clock-tracking filters, bucket noise, a resonant feedback tilt, freeze, a feedback governor and an input high-pass.
presentation.overview: The mono sum goes through a BBD chain: an optional input high-pass, a tanh into a 2:1 feedback compressor, an 8th-order anti-alias filter at a third of the clock, a bucket line clocked at 5.1 to 20.5 kHz with a charge-transfer polynomial and noise, a 9th-order reconstruction filter and the expander. FDBK returns the wet through a tilt with a sweepable bandpass; LIM governs how loud self-oscillation gets; FRZ holds the line. TIME glides the clock, so moving it bends the pitch of the line. The dry signal is never processed.
highlights: The clock sets the delay: longer repeats are darker and grainier, as on a BBD chip
TIME glides the clock over 20 ms: locks and LFOs bend the pitch of the repeats
1,023 or 4,095 buckets: 50 to 200 ms (the default) or 200 to 800 ms
TONE right of centre: a treble shelf; left: a resonant bandpass that FREQ places at 400 Hz-2 kHz
FRZ: from longer trails to an endless loop of the line, made for the crossfader
LIM keeps self-oscillation at a set level; HPF cuts bass into the line, 20 to 400 Hz
MIX 0 is the exact dry signal
usage: Choose BBD DELAY in FX2 SETUP: hold FUNC, press FX2, turn LEVEL to the end of the list and press YES. The SETUP page holds STGS (bucket count) on encoder A, LIM on C and HPF on E.
On the main page: TIME (A), FDBK (B), FRZ (C), TONE (D), FREQ (E) and MIX (F).
With TONE towards either end the loop rings on from about FDBK 40; LIM (default 127, strongest) sets how loud it gets, and TIME or FREQ then sweep it.
The six main-page knobs take parameter locks, LFOs, scenes and MIDI CC like any stock effect's; the SETUP knobs are set per Part.

controls.name: TIME
controls.doc: The bucket clock, 20.5 kHz at 0 to 5.1 kHz at 127, linear in delay time and gliding over 20 ms. The delay is 50-200 ms (STGS 1024) or 200-800 ms (4096). Not tempo-synced.

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: The wet returned to the input through TONE. With TONE centred the repeats ring longer up to 127 (about 1 dB a second) but never self-oscillate; with TONE at either end the loop rings on from about FDBK 40, at a level LIM sets.

controls.name: FRZ
controls.doc: Freeze: rising from 0 the input fades out of the line and FDBK goes towards sustain for the current TONE (never down), so trails lengthen; at 127 the line loops its contents exactly at the level it had, ignoring input and FDBK. Crossfades of any speed into 127 keep the level. TIME changes the frozen loop's speed and pitch; a STGS change clears it.

controls.name: TONE
controls.doc: Bipolar, centre flat. The feedback tilt, 9 dB at the ends: right raises treble and cuts bass about 200 Hz; left adds a bandpass peak at FREQ, Q 1.5. Acts only inside the feedback loop.

controls.name: FREQ
controls.doc: The centre of TONE's bandpass, 400 Hz to 2 kHz, logarithmic; 64 is about 900 Hz. Heard only with TONE left of centre; right of centre it does nothing.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: 0 is exactly dry. To 64 the wet rises to unity over the whole dry; from 64 to 127 the dry fades out, leaving the wet alone.

controls.name: STGS
controls.doc: SETUP page, encoder A. Bucket count, so the delay range: 1024 (default) gives 50-200 ms, 4096 gives 200-800 ms. A change fades the wet out, clears the line (about 6 ms, dry) and fades back in. Not lockable (SETUP page).

controls.name: LIM
controls.doc: SETUP page, encoder C. The feedback governor, 0 off, 127 (default) strongest: above a threshold of the wet's envelope FDBK is scaled by the square of the overshoot, so self-oscillation settles about 30 dB under LIM 0.

controls.name: HPF
controls.doc: SETUP page, encoder E. 0 is off. Otherwise a 12 dB/octave Butterworth high-pass on the signal entering the bucket line, 20 Hz at 1 to 400 Hz at 127, logarithmic (64 is about 90 Hz); it glides like FREQ.

limitations: Hardware: on the owner's MKII over USB (15 October 2026): install, both cores, two instances on core 1, Part switches, removal and reinstall, the stop kill and its release, chip load. MKI, MIDI load, project save and reload and a power cycle on this version, and the card build's stop-kill hook on hardware are untested.

On today's beta base a DSP core holds BBD's 1,112 words beside what the bank's Parts keep loaded there: core 0 (T5-T8) has 2,361 words, so a bank whose Parts keep DARK REV on T5-T8 refuses BBD there (DSP MEMORY FULL); core 1 (T1-T4) has 3,234. One instance a core fits the DSP budget beside seven stock effects; a second fits on core 1 only.
Over USB it needs the Modwerk beta base with the ev_tail_kill event (ba89721d or later) and keeps its card effect id, 14: a set where another module holds id 14 is refused.
FX2 only: the bucket line needs the 16K-word delay buffer the OS gives FX2 instances.

Aliasing is the bucket brigade's own: -44 dBc for a 1.1 kHz tone at the fastest clock, -37 dBc at the slowest.

conditions.parameterModulation: Two calls per 16-frame block cover trigger splits, each charged the full per-call bound. LFOs, locks, scenes and CC reach the same knob words. No contention or silicon wall-clock timing is claimed.
conditions.modeSwitching: STGS changes (fade, clear, reset), FRZ 127, HPF on and off and the hidden stop-kill input (dry and clear) are inside the union bound.
conditions.maxLoad: Eight FX2 instances, four per DSP core, at 44.1 kHz and 16 frames per block: 44,992 per core within the SDK 49,920 module allowance; the stock/scheduling reserve stays separate. presentation.label: RING / SHIFT / CRUSH
presentation.summary: One modulator, ring mod or a stereo frequency shifter, followed by sample-rate and bit reduction on stock LO-FI's curves and a high-shelf cut.
presentation.overview: LOFI2 is an insert on its own effect ID, so stock LO-FI stays in the chooser beside it. MODE picks the modulator: RING multiplies the track by a carrier, DOWN and UP shift every partial by FREQ Hz with a stereo Hilbert pair. MIX is the modulator's depth; SRR and BRR run after it on stock LO-FI's measured rates and curve and stay live at MIX 0, and LPF is a -12 dB high shelf last in the chain. Every continuous knob glides to its new value over about 1.5 ms. The defaults are a passthrough.
highlights: Ring modulator with an exponential six-octave FREQ, LOW/HIGH range and L/R carrier phase
Stereo frequency shifter, up or down, with feedback
SRR and BRR matched to stock LO-FI in a native render (rates within 0.02 dB of droop, steps within 0.01 bit)
Passthrough at defaults; every continuous knob glides, no zipper steps above -70 dBFS in the render gate
usage: On an audio track that plays a sample, hold FUNC and press FX2, turn LEVEL to LOFI2 and press YES. Nothing changes yet: the defaults are a passthrough.

Press FX2 for the main page. Turn MIX (encoder B) to 127 and FREQ (encoder A) to 64: the track is ring-modulated. Raise SRR or BRR (encoders D and E) for sample-rate and bit reduction, and lower LPF (encoder F) from 127 to darken the result.

For the frequency shifter, hold FUNC and press FX2 and turn MODE (encoder C) to UP or DOWN; on the main page the third knob is now FDBK. To bypass, set MIX, SRR and BRR to 0 and LPF to 127, or choose NONE in FX2 SETUP.

controls.name: FREQ
controls.doc: Modulator frequency, exponential over six octaves from RNGE's base. RING: 2-130 Hz (LOW) or 60-4,000 Hz (HIGH). SHIFT: 2-128 Hz (LOW) or 31.25-2,000 Hz (HIGH). FREQ 0 is the base frequency, not silence.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Modulator depth: crossfades the ring or shift output against the dry signal. Not a global wet/dry: SRR, BRR and LPF still act at MIX 0.

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: One knob, renamed by MODE. In DOWN and UP it is FDBK, the shifter's feedback (a ladder at f, f+d, f+2d), capped at 0.40 (0.45 before 0.1.1, where the top of FDBK could sustain itself). In RING the panel shows GAIN: make-up on the ring product, 0 dB at 0, +6 dB at 64, +11.9 dB at 127.

controls.name: SRR
controls.doc: Sample-rate reduction at stock LO-FI's measured rates: no reduction through 7, 8,018 Hz at 64, 3,564 Hz at 127. 0 is off.

controls.name: BRR
controls.doc: Bit-depth reduction on stock LO-FI's curve, round-to-nearest: about 13.5 bits removed at 64 and 20.8 at 127. 0 is full depth.

controls.name: LPF
controls.doc: High-shelf cut, last in the chain: -12 dB above a corner swept from 100 Hz at 0 to 16 kHz at 126. 127 takes it out of circuit bit for bit; turn down to darken.

controls.name: RNGE
controls.doc: FREQ's range (RNGE on the panel): LOW is sub-audio (tremolo in RING, slow swirl in SHIFT), HIGH is the audio range.

controls.name: MODE
controls.doc: RING is the ring modulator; DOWN and UP are the frequency shifter moving every partial down or up. Ring and shift are exclusive. A change ducks the modulator for 5 ms each way so it does not click.

controls.name: AMPH
controls.doc: Ring carrier's L/R phase offset, bipolar: -90 to +88.6 degrees, 0 at the centre. + puts R ahead. RING only.

Large: 838 program words and a 516-word table on each DSP core, 1,354 contiguous words. With stock DSP code built in it needs two adjacent stock reverbs given up (PLATE REV + SPRING REV, or SPRING REV + DARK REV); one reverb is not enough.

SHIFT executes 430 instructions/sample at worst in dsp_host (static 416 cycles), about 1.4x SPRING REV's worst case and dearer than every stock effect; RING is 274. The author ran eight instances at once, four per core, in UP, DOWN and RING on his MKII in his own build (build 12, the 21f6de90 instructions), and eight in SHIFT DOWN with FX1 empty in build 16 (this source).

Over USB the Modwerk base loads LOFI2 on demand into FX1 or FX2. It declares 637 cycles a sample (timed on an MKII with package 7ee9277f of 21f6de90, whose instructions are the same; only data words differ), so two instances fit on one DSP core when its other slots are free and a third is refused (DSP FULL).

In DOWN and UP, once sound has passed through, the output settles at about -83 to -94 dBFS instead of silence and stays there (dsp_host render; the upstream module does the same). RING and the reduction stages return to silence.

Native octabam refuses LOFI2 together with Analog BD: it is not on Analog BD's reviewed DSP companion list. A scratch-only probe with the list widened placed both only with all three reverbs, LO-FI, DJ EQ and CHORUS given up and LOFI2's table moved to X memory; that layout is unreviewed and untested.

In a card build only the FX2 chooser was built and captured, and FX1 in a card image was not run on a unit. Over USB the base loads it into FX1 as well; FX1 ran on an MKII with 21f6de90's USB package (7ee9277f), not with 0.1.0's or 0.1.1's.

Effect ID 0x09, placement priority 19 and layout letter F are Modwerk's; they were checked free against the modules in this tree. A project saved with octabam's LOFI2 (ID 0x1f) selects TAPEHEAD's ID here.

Four LOFI2 in SHIFT on one DSP core with an effect on FX1 can lock the unit: on the author's MKII, four in SHIFT on T5-T8 with FILTER on FX1 of T5-T8 locked it, on upstream main as well (0.1.0 is affected too; https://github.com/sambanks/octabam/issues/850, open, no guard yet). Eight in SHIFT DOWN with FX1 empty ran. Over USB the base admits at most two per core (637 declared cycles); a card build has no such guard, and the count at which it starts with FX1 in use is not known yet.
No single-knob bypass: a passthrough is MIX 0, SRR 0, BRR 0 and LPF 127, the defaults.
A parameter lock holds until the track's next trig, as it does for every stock parameter on this OS.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: ring, crush and shift a loop
steps: On an audio track that plays a sample, hold FUNC and press FX2, turn LEVEL to LOFI2 and press YES. Nothing changes yet: the defaults are a passthrough.

Press FX2 for the main page. Turn MIX (encoder B) to 127 and FREQ (encoder A) to 64: the track is ring-modulated. Raise SRR or BRR (encoders D and E) for sample-rate and bit reduction, and lower LPF (encoder F) from 127 to darken the result.

For the frequency shifter, hold FUNC and press FX2 and turn MODE (encoder C) to UP or DOWN; on the main page the third knob is now FDBK. To bypass, set MIX, SRR and BRR to 0 and LPF to 127, or choose NONE in FX2 SETUP.

conditions.parameterExtremes: tools/build/cycle_count.py prices the dearest path of the per-sample loop, SHIFT, at 416 cycles/sample; RING is cheaper. perf.py bench ran the manifest's dearest settings (every continuous knob at its costly end, LPF in band) in SHIFT UP, SHIFT DOWN and RING, the defaults, and the fixed and moving patterns: worst 430.06 executed instructions/sample.
conditions.parameterModulation: The moving pattern changes every active slot at every 16-sample block; the stress run adds three LFOs per track and a new value on every slot each sixteenth. LFOs, parameter locks, MIDI CC and scenes all arrive as the same knob words. A parameter lock was tried on a unit with 21f6de90 (the same instructions); scenes were not confirmed on a unit.
conditions.modeSwitching: The stress run redraws MODE and RNGE every sixteenth, so RING, DOWN and UP switch under load with the 5 ms duck; a trig split at every position 1-15 is in the benchmark (worst at 1). Re-selection runs init once. MODE was switched by hand on a unit with 0.1.0's source (8250be0c) and with 21f6de90; with 0.1.1's the tester reported the functions passing without per-mode detail; Part changes were not measured.
conditions.maxLoad: Four instances per core on FX2 of all eight tracks, behind DJ EQ (the dearest stock effect) on every FX1: 4 x 416 = 1,664 of 3,120 usable static cycles per core. dsp_host stress, 32 s, -guard -dirty: no hang, no clobber. Five SHIFT instances ran at once on a unit with 21f6de90; two on one core with 0.1.0's source (8250be0c); one with 0.1.1's. Hardware contradicts this load with FX1 occupied: the author's MKII locked with four SHIFT instances on T5-T8 and FILTER on FX1 of T5-T8, on upstream main as well (octabam issue 850, open; 4 x 416 + 4 x 192 = 2,432 static cycles, inside the model's budget). Streaming, USB and MIDI load are not in the model.

presentation.label: RINGMOD SC
presentation.summary: Ring mod sidechain: another track's level ducks this one, or its waveform ring-modulates, steps, rectifies or tremolos it.
presentation.overview: Put it on the track to be ducked and choose the KEY track. In DUCK the gain follows the key's peak, holding through the kick's zero crossings and recovering as it decays; in RING the key multiplies the audio, and S&H, RECT and SLEW shape that carrier. The key comes from the Modwerk base's key bus over USB, so it needs no other module and runs beside Sidechain Compressor.
highlights: DUCK: gain = 1 - DPTH x follow(peak of |key| over 13-26 ms): no buzz at the kick's zero crossings
A fixed 4x key boost brings a full-scale key track at the default AMP VOL to full (measured under the emulator)
RING: a ring modulator whose carrier is any of T1-T8
RING's S&H steps the carrier, RECT rectifies it (frequency doubled), SLEW turns it into the key's level (tremolo)
KEY is the first knob of the main page, so it can be locked and modulated
Reads the base's key bus (USB): no tap of its own, so it runs beside Sidechain Compressor
DPTH 0, KEY OFF or no key bus returns the input bit for bit
usage: Select RINGMOD SC on FX1 or FX2 of the track to duck and turn KEY (encoder A) to the kick's track; DPTH sets how deep.
Raise REL for a slower recovery and ATK to soften the onset; turn KLPF to about 30-50 so only the kick's body drives the duck.

MODE on the SETUP page switches to RING, where the key track multiplies the audio: turn S&H and RECT to 0 for the plain ring modulator, then raise S&H for steps, RECT for a rectified, frequency-doubled carrier and SLEW for a tremolo that follows the key.

controls.name: KEY
controls.doc: The track whose audio drives the gain; OFF = untouched.

controls.name: DPTH
controls.doc: How far the key moves the gain; 0 = untouched, 127 = full.

controls.name: KLPF
controls.doc: Low-pass on the key: 14 Hz at 0, an octave every 14 steps (about 100 Hz at 40), open at 127.

controls.name: ATK
controls.doc: DUCK: how slowly the gain falls; 0 is at once, then about 0.7 ms at 1 to 1.3 s at 127, doubling every 11.6 steps. RING (SLEW): 0 rings with the key itself; above 0 the key's level, smoothed over the same times, drives the gain (a tremolo that follows the key).

controls.name: HOLD
controls.doc: DUCK: how long the duck holds after each peak of the key, one to two windows of 32 + 16v samples (13 ms at 34, 0.7 ms at 0, 47 ms at 127). RING (S&H): a new key every 16v samples, held between (0 every sample, 0.36 ms at 1, 12 ms at 34, 46 ms at 127).

controls.name: REL
controls.doc: DUCK: how slowly the gain recovers once the key's peak drops, on ATK's scale (45 about 9 ms, 64 about 31 ms, 96 about 210 ms). RING (RECT): blends the key toward its rectified |key|; 0 is the key, 127 fully rectified (frequency doubled, never negative: an AM-like modulation).

controls.name: MODE
controls.doc: DUCK: the key's level pulls the gain down. RING: the key multiplies the audio. ATK, HOLD and REL read SLEW, S&H and RECT in RING.

limitations: Needs the Modwerk base's key bus, which only the USB base has (loader ABI 9, `requires keybus`), so it is USB-only: the configurator refuses card firmware with it (the site's rule for a package that requires a base feature). A card image built with it anyway has no key bus, and there the effect keeps its depth at 0 and passes the audio untouched.

While RINGMOD SC is installed the base's tap copies every track's audio on every block, on both cores, and its price (41 executed instructions a sample a core, charged at 7/4) counts toward RINGMOD SC, even with no instance on a track. That figure is counted from the tap's source; the chip cost is not measured.
The key is taken before the key track's own effects.

The key is exact when its track is dispatched before this one on the same DSP core (T1-T4, T5-T8), 16 samples late when after, and 32 samples late across the cores (the key bus's latency, measured on an MKII for Sidechain Compressor; not yet with this module).
A MODE or KEY change fades the effect out, clears the key's state and fades back in over about 1 ms, so a KEY parameter lock shorter than that is not heard.
Installing or reinstalling Sidechain Compressor while RINGMOD SC is live re-zeroes the key bus once: up to about a block of silent key (by design of the base, not measured with this module).

On a base from before the module select step fix (on main's beta base since 22 October 2026), KEY may move one track per detent on the first visit to the main page after choosing the effect, until the page is entered again. With the fix, on the MKII development twin on 22 October 2026, it stepped cleanly from the first visit.

Declared conflict with Analog BD: carried over from the card builder's rule (Analog BD admits only the effects on its companion list, and this one is not on it). Over USB no resource clash is known; it is declared for every build until the owner decides otherwise, so the configurator never offers both.

DUCK buzzes at its very shortest settings: with ATK, HOLD and REL all near 0 the gain follows each cycle of the key, an audio-rate amplitude modulation (heard on an MKII with 0.1.0, as expected). Keep HOLD above half a cycle of the key for a clean duck.

A slow SLEW stops a little short of the key's level (each sample's rise is truncated to the word; up to about 1.4% of full scale at 127, as the review measured on the build before) and a very quiet key never raises it from 0; an LFO on S&H turns S&H 0 into a hold of 1 to 15 samples.

On an MKII (22 October 2026, over USB, a development twin of the beta base) DUCK, RING and its three knobs (SLEW turned through 0), two instances, Part and project reload and every install and removal order beside Sidechain Compressor were checked. Parameter locks and LFOs, scenes and the crossfader, eight instances a core and a power cycle are not tested on a unit.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Put a kick on T1 and a sustained bass on T2. Select T2, hold FUNC and press FX1, turn LEVEL to RINGMOD SC and press YES, then press FX1.
Turn encoder A until KEY reads T1. The bass dips with every kick and comes back as the kick decays; DPTH (encoder B) sets how deep.

Raise REL (encoder F) for a slower recovery, HOLD (encoder E) for a longer pump and ATK (encoder D) to soften the onset. Turn KLPF (encoder C) down to about 30-50 so only the kick's body drives the duck, not its click or other sounds on the key track.
Turn KEY back to OFF, or DPTH to 0, to hear the bass untouched.

For RING, hold FUNC and press FX1, set MODE to RING and press FX1 again. Turn S&H (encoder E) and RECT (encoder F) to 0: the bass is ring-modulated by the kick. Raise S&H for a stepped, sample-and-hold carrier, RECT for a rectified, frequency-doubled carrier, and SLEW (encoder D) to about 40-60 for a tremolo that follows the kick's level. Choose NONE in SETUP to remove the effect.

Connect and route: connect the Octatrack USB port to Outbox 8. In Elektron's Outbox app, match Main / USB 1/2 to physical outputs 1/2 and Cue / USB 3/4 to physical outputs 3/4. Modwerk stores this plan; it does not program the Outbox hardware.

Use and reset: Main is the final stereo mix; Cue is the separate stereo Cue bus. Outputs 5/6 and 7/8 are off. To use different signals, change and save the source and assignments, rebuild, and update the external app. Stop the stream before changing cabling.

presentation.label: SCALE / ROOT
presentation.summary: Keep pitch edits and chromatic trig keys in one of 24 scales with a selectable root.
presentation.overview: Scale Quantizer adds SCALE, ROOT and GLIDE to PROJECT > CONTROL > SEQUENCER. Pitch turns and parameter locks move through scale degrees, and chromatic trig keys snap to the chosen scale. ROOT transposes the scale and keyboard. SCALE OFF restores stock pitch behavior.
highlights: 24 scales plus OFF
Selectable root C–B
Pitch knob, parameter locks and chromatic keys follow the scale
usage: Open PROJECT > CONTROL > SEQUENCER and set SCALE. OFF preserves stock pitch behavior; choose a scale to constrain notes.
Set ROOT to the key you want. Pitch edits step by scale degree; chromatic keys snap to a degree and key 1 plays the root.
SCALE, ROOT and GLIDE persist through project save/reload and battery RAM. Synth polyphony and synth glide features require SYNTH MACHINE, which is outside this import.

access.location: Audio track > FUNC+SRC > FM SYNTH; SRC for tone, LFO for voices/chords, FUNC+AMP for LEG.
steps: Open a disposable project with FM Synth firmware. Select an audio track, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FM SYNTH with UP/DOWN and press YES. No sample is required.
Press SRC. Set RATO to 1 and turn INDX from 0 upwards to hear a sine tone acquire FM harmonics. PTCH transposes it; FINE tunes it in cents; FDBK adds feedback; DEC shortens the modulation envelope.
Place a trig and press PLAY. Press LFO to set VOIC to 2–4 and CHRD to a chord if wanted. AMP ATK/HOLD/REL shape the gain envelope; FUNC+AMP exposes LEG.
Press STOP twice to silence the voice. To return to a sample machine, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FLEX or STATIC and press YES; assign the desired sample in the normal way.
For scales and glide, open PROJECT > CONTROL > SEQUENCER. Select SCALE, ROOT or GLIDE with UP/DOWN and turn LEVEL. SCALE OFF restores unquantized pitch.

presentation.label: Two-operator FM
presentation.summary: Two-operator FM with a dedicated track machine, one to four voices, chords and glide.
presentation.overview: FM SYNTH provides one to four paraphonic FM voices through the stock AMP and effects. Version 0.1.2 preserves the MIDI chromatic drawer stack and adds 18.06 dB source headroom. Software regression and native/browser composition checks pass. The owner approved release without current hardware validation; chip timing and complete memory bounds remain unknown. The original static symptom remains unconfirmed on hardware.
highlights: Dedicated machine chooser entry; no sample required.
Pitch, ratio, index, fine tuning, feedback and index decay on SRC.
One to four paraphonic voices, chord shapes and inversions.
Chromatic playing, MIDI, legato and privately bundled scale/glide controls.
usage: Open a disposable project with FM Synth firmware. Select an audio track, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FM SYNTH with UP/DOWN and press YES. No sample is required.
Press SRC. Set RATO to 1 and turn INDX from 0 upwards to hear a sine tone acquire FM harmonics. PTCH transposes it; FINE tunes it in cents; FDBK adds feedback; DEC shortens the modulation envelope.
Place a trig and press PLAY. Press LFO to set VOIC to 2–4 and CHRD to a chord if wanted. AMP ATK/HOLD/REL shape the gain envelope; FUNC+AMP exposes LEG.
Press STOP twice to silence the voice. To return to a sample machine, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FLEX or STATIC and press YES; assign the desired sample in the normal way.

controls.name: PTCH
controls.doc: SRC A: raw 64 is 0 semitones; raw 0–127 gives −64…+63. Scale and chromatic edits can constrain pitch.

controls.name: RATO
controls.doc: SRC B: raw>>2 selects 32 modulation ratios from 0.25 to 16; default raw 12 gives ratio 1.

controls.name: INDX
controls.doc: SRC C: FM modulation depth, raw 0–127. Zero produces the unmodulated carrier.

controls.name: FINE
controls.doc: SRC D: raw 64 is 0 cents; raw 0–127 gives −64…+63 cents.

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: SRC E: modulation-operator feedback, raw 0–127. Extreme feedback can be bright and alias.

controls.name: DEC
controls.doc: SRC F: modulation-index decay. Default raw 40 displays about 199 ms. This is separate from the AMP gain envelope.

controls.name: VOIC
controls.doc: LFO C: effective voice count 1–4. Values outside 1–4, including raw 0, normalize to one voice. Initial inherited LFO value displays one; four voices share the track filter and AMP.

controls.name: CHRD
controls.doc: LFO F: 32 chord shapes with four inversions each, encoded as shape<<2 | inversion. ---- uses individual played/recorded notes.

controls.name: LEG
controls.doc: FUNC+AMP F: OFF retriggers, MONO preserves one envelope across overlapping keys, POLY enables paraphonic legato. Ordinary sample tracks expose OFF/MONO.

controls.name: SCALE
controls.doc: OFF restores stock pitch behavior; select a scale to constrain PTCH edits, locks and chromatic keys.

controls.name: ROOT
controls.doc: Root of the scale and chromatic keyboard. Ignored with SCALE OFF.

controls.name: GLIDE
controls.doc: OFF or 1–127 slide time; the track LEG setting controls legato.

limitations: Parts store stock FLEX kind 1 plus FM/1 in unused NEIGHBOR control bytes. A stock build reads the track as FLEX; it does not synthesize FM. Choose stock explicitly before downgrading.
LFO3 speed/depth become VOIC/CHRD; LFO3 depth is muted. ATK/HOLD/REL remain inherited stock AMP controls and drive the synth’s own envelope.
ATK 0 with a short HOLD or REL starts and stops each voice abruptly and can click; raise ATK a few steps or lengthen REL (#557).
LFO1/LFO2 destinations keep FLEX's names: STRT is RATO, LEN is INDX, RATE is FINE, RTRG is FDBK, RTIM is DEC (#589). Whether LFOs on them change the FM sound is not tested.
The matching quantizer is bundled privately because the engine shares its mailbox and fixed scale accessor. Do not also select the public Scale Quantizer.

Cannot combine with Analog BD or the public Scale Quantizer because their native hooks overlap. Compatible mixed builds have native/browser byte-parity evidence; mixed audio loads have not been stress-tested.

MIDI selector recovery and one-track mono/four-voice playback are emulator-tested. External MIDI note/CC traffic, saved project/Part reloads, legato, modulation, maximum simultaneous tracks and hardware timing remain unqualified.
Historical upstream marker-FLEX activation remains for compatibility; the verified route is the dedicated FM SYNTH chooser.

Source output is 18.06 dB quieter at identical mixer settings. Added headroom mitigates gain clipping; effects, resonant filtering and summed tracks can still clip. The hardware static report has not been reproduced.

controls.name: ATK
controls.doc: Stock attack control, raw 0-127; determines how quickly compression engages. Exact time mapping is inherited from stock.

controls.name: REL
controls.doc: Stock release control, raw 0-127; determines recovery after detector level falls.

controls.name: THRS
controls.doc: Stock threshold, raw 0-127; lower it until the selected key causes gain reduction.

controls.name: RAT
controls.doc: Stock compression ratio, raw 0-127; raise it to increase compression.

controls.name: GAIN
controls.doc: Stock output make-up gain, raw 0-127. This is distinct from KGN, which changes the detector input.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Stock dry/wet balance, raw 0-127; 127 is fully processed and 0 is dry.

controls.name: RMS
controls.doc: Stock RMS detector control, raw 0-127; retained on page 2 without changing its implementation.

controls.name: KEY
controls.doc: OFF restores self-keyed stock detection; 1-8 selects absolute T1-T8, including tracks on the other DSP core.

controls.name: KFLT
controls.doc: 0-63 low-pass; 64 bypass; 65-127 high-pass. LCD shows LP/OFF/HP. One-pole filter uses a 32-entry 40-2200 Hz table and special near-bypass edges; no exact cutoff readout.

controls.name: KGN
controls.doc: Raw 0-127 about unity at 64. Sixteen 8-value buckets yield -24 to +21 dB in 3 dB steps; the gain is smoothed with a nominal 5 ms block-rate time constant. LCD displays the stock bipolar raw offset, not dB.

controls.name: MON
controls.doc: OFF is normal compression; ON plays the processed key on this receiving track instead of its output, after both effects. MON requires a selected KEY.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: duck T5 from a T1 kick
steps: Back up the project, work on a disposable copy, and put a kick on T1 and a sustained sample or loop on T5. Build with Modwerk; with Keep stock FX2 effects on, SPRING REV gives up its code space, so reassign any track that used it.

controls.name: TYPE
controls.doc: 0–15. Low values favor varied scale notes; higher values prefer tonic/fifth and stronger beat positions. Original algorithm; not a byte-identical Sting port.

controls.name: DENS
controls.doc: 0–16. Note count is round(motif length × DENS / 16). Zero is silence; 16 fills the motif. Changes commit immediately with the current seed.

controls.name: ROOT
controls.doc: C–B. Sample reference is C at neutral PTCH. Tune the source sample accordingly. Pitch locks stay within −12 to +12 semitones.

controls.name: SCAL
controls.doc: Chromatic, natural minor, major, Dorian or minor pentatonic. All generated pitches remain in the selected scale.

controls.name: GATE
controls.doc: 0–126 in native AMP HOLD units, not percent or milliseconds. Generated HOLD locks range from half to all of this value. AMP REL still shapes the audible tail.

controls.name: ACNT
controls.doc: 0–127. Strong notes keep the Part AMP VOL. Other notes are attenuated by up to half; zero gives equal volumes. This writes AMP VOL locks, not MIDI velocity.

controls.name: SEED
controls.doc: 0–127. Select the deterministic variation; YES advances and wraps this value. Other parameter edits keep it fixed.

controls.name: SPAN
controls.doc: 0–12 semitones either side of OFST, clipped to the native ±12-semitone range. Pitches remain in the selected scale; an empty window uses its nearest scale note.

controls.name: OFST
controls.doc: Displayed as −12 to +12 semitones; stored midpoint 12 means zero. Moves the center of the pitch window.

controls.name: ROT
controls.doc: 0–63 steps. Rotate the generated phrase right within the native track length.

controls.name: RPT
controls.doc: OFF (0) uses the full native track length. 1–64 chooses a repeating motif; larger values are clipped to the active length.

controls.name: DIR
controls.doc: FWD or REV. Reverse the generated phrase before applying ROT.

tutorial.title: Generate a phrase, then edit a note
steps: Select an audio track. Open SRC page 2 (double-tap SRC), choose VECTOR and press YES. In the backing-pool modal, highlight STATIC or FLEX with UP/DOWN or LEVEL, then press RIGHT to enter that pool. YES also opens the highlighted pool; YES on a loaded sample slot assigns that pool and sample to VECTOR. Use the corresponding stock sample-slot and file-loading tools to load a tuned sample; NO returns from the sample browser.

Double-tap the assigned TRACK to reopen the pool modal. LEFT returns to the machine list; RIGHT on VECTOR opens the modal. RIGHT in the pool modal opens the highlighted Static/Flex sample list. In a sample-slot list, LEFT returns to pool choice and RIGHT opens the stock file browser. Horizontal arrows navigate menus without changing the assigned pool; YES on a sample slot commits the pool and sample.
Press SRC for TYPE, DENS, ROOT, SCAL, GATE and ACNT on encoders A–F. Turn a parameter to commit a phrase immediately, including during playback. The current seed stays fixed while shaping the vector.
Open SRC page 2 with a double tap on SRC. Encoders A–F adjust SEED, SPAN, OFST, ROT, RPT and DIR. These changes also commit immediately; press SRC to return.

Press PLAY to hear the native sequencer repeat the phrase. Push LEVEL on SRC for the ordinary sample controls, then use grid recording and a held trig to edit PTCH. AMP exposes the generated HOLD/VOL locks. Push LEVEL again to return.
Press YES on the generator for a new seed and variation. STOP/PLAY preserves a populated phrase. Select normal FLEX/STATIC to remove VECTOR while retaining the generated pattern.

presentation.label: PLAYHEAD DIRECTION
presentation.summary: Play patterns reversed, pingpong, random or shuffled, or hold trig keys to repeat steps: per pattern, shared by every track or set per track.
presentation.overview: Play Modes changes which step the sequencer plays at each position: NORMAL, REVERSED, PINGPONG (end steps once), PINGPONG 2 (end steps twice), RANDOM or SHUFFLE. Each pattern keeps its own modes: one shared mode under SCALE MODE NORMAL, one per audio and MIDI track under PER TRACK. Trigs, conditions, micro-timing, swing and locks move with their step; tempo, lengths, chains and the trig LEDs stay in step. The modes are saved with the project, survive a power cycle and follow pattern copy, paste and clear. REPEAT plays normally until trig keys are held while playing; then the track loops only the held steps, and on release it continues from where the stock playhead has reached.
highlights: Six playhead modes, including two pingpongs and a shuffle that plays every step once per pass
STEP REPEAT: hold trig keys to loop those steps, let go to land back in time
Per pattern; per track under PER TRACK scale mode, audio and MIDI tracks
Hold a TRACK key and press UP or DOWN; a popup names the mode
Saved in the project, kept over a power cycle, carried by pattern copy and paste
usage: Hold a TRACK key and press DOWN to step through NORMAL, REVERSED, PINGPONG, PINGPONG 2, RANDOM, SHUFFLE and REPEAT; UP walks back. The popup shows ALL <mode> under SCALE MODE NORMAL, or T1..T8 / M1..M8 <mode> under PER TRACK.
In REPEAT, press PLAY and hold trig keys: the track loops the held steps in step order; let go and it continues from where it would have been.
Each pattern keeps its own modes; PLAY and every pattern change start the tracks from their first step again.
Under PER TRACK, MASTER LENGTH limits how far a track gets; set it to INF to let every track run its full length in every mode.

limitations: Does not combine with octabam's PLOCKS P2 (not in this catalog): both use battery RAM 0x100f8600.. and the 20 pattern-copy memcpy sites.

limitations: Experimental release: physical CPU deadlines, recording, reboot persistence and broader stock workflows remain unqualified.

Voices are limited by CPU time: POLY8 plays fewer voices when its rendering would take more than 40 % of the CPU on average, about 197 us of one audio frame, or starve the panel. On the current beta base (module code uncached) that is about three voices with one POLY8 track; on a base with cached module code seven to eight.
Only one newly assigned POLY8 machine per Part; older multi-POLY8 Parts must be reduced to one before use. Fixed headroom makes a single note 18.06 dB quieter than 0.2.1.
TSTR is OFF while POLY8 is active.
FLEX only; STATIC requires independent streaming-cache support.
Panel recording supports up to four notes within an octave; wider/larger chords and recorded key-up duration are unsupported. Extended-range MIDI recording remains incomplete.
MIDI channels shared with non-POLY8 audio tracks keep stock note-command mapping outside 72–96.
Linear interpolation can alias at high pitches; no anti-aliasing upgrade is claimed.
Ratios saturate below 32× rather than fold by octaves; very low pitches are limited by Q16 playback phase.
The octave selector is a global live control; it is not saved per Part.
Recorded chord steps use PTCH lock storage for their root. Stock PTCH lock editing/display for those steps is not qualified; native SAMPLE locks remain available.
Shared-machine composition is covered by guarded dispatch seams; native memory and DSP limits can still refuse a selection.

presentation.label: Any track to MAIN, CUE or PHONES
presentation.summary: Turn the headphone jack into a third assignable output pair and pick each track's outputs with CUE + LEVEL.
presentation.overview: Adds MATRIX beside NORMAL and STUDIO in PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO (the box stock calls CUE CFG, titled OUT CFG with the module). In MATRIX, LEVEL sets a track's level and CUE + LEVEL chooses where it plays: MAIN, CUE or PHONES as stereo pairs in any combination, or a single mono jack of the six (track L+R summed at half each, so a centred sound keeps its level). The choice is stored in the Part, so it survives SRC page resets, Part reload and project save. The MIXER's MIX knob becomes the PHONES output level. Inputs keep their stock DIR routing to MAIN.
highlights: Three stereo output pairs: MAIN, CUE and the headphone jack.
Per track: any combination of MAIN, CUE and PHONES, or one mono jack (MAIN L/R, CUE L/R, PHONES L/R).
Routing lives in the Part: SRC page resets and track clears leave it alone.
With MASTER TRACK on, tracks routed to MAIN feed the master and track 8's destination picks where the master plays.
usage: PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO: select OUT CFG > MATRIX and press YES.
On a track, the LEV box is labelled with the destination (MN, PHN, ...). Hold CUE and turn LEVEL to change it.
In the MIXER, MIX (labelled PHN) sets the PHONES output level. Choose NORMAL or STUDIO again to return to stock behaviour.

limitations: Builds with the stock DSP code built in and takes a given-up stock effect's program memory on core 0. The builder chooses it: SPRING REV first, then PLATE REV or DARK REV when other modules also need room. The given-up effect leaves the FX2 menu.
The MATRIX mixdown costs core 0 up to about 208 more instructions per sample than stock (every track on ALL, MASTER on, bus levels moving); every track on MAIN adds about 20.
Switching to or from MATRIX rewrites every Part's LEVEL and cue bytes (and, into NORMAL, the project's cue settings) by documented rules; save to keep it.
A MATRIX project opened on a stock OS loads as STUDIO with tiny cue levels; switch to NORMAL or STUDIO before flashing another OS.
Changes core 0's mixdown and headphone crossfade; other modules that hook those sites are refused by the ledger.
Not yet combinable with Analog BD, whose builder places DSP code only beside a reviewed list of effects.

access.location: Any audio-track page, with SCENE A, SCENE B or both held; for p-locks, grid recording with trigs held.
steps: Lock parameters in SCENE A and SCENE B as usual (hold the scene key and turn knobs).

presentation.label: Apply Scene
presentation.summary: Hold SCENE A or SCENE B and press YES: that scene's locked values become the active Part's own. Hold both and press YES to keep the crossfader's current blend. In grid recording, hold trigs and press a scene key (or both) to write the same values as p-locks on those steps.
presentation.overview: Keep a scene, or keep a blend. SCENE A + YES writes every value scene A locks into the active Part, as if you had turned each knob there yourself; SCENE B + YES does the same for scene B. Hold both scene keys and press YES to write the sound the crossfader plays right now instead. The scenes, the crossfader and the saved Part stay as they were, so the scenes keep morphing from the new base and RELOAD PART takes you back to the last saved Part. In grid recording the same gesture works on steps: hold trigs, press SCENE A, SCENE B or both, and let go; the values become p-locks on the held steps of the active track.
highlights: Covers every scene-lockable page on all eight audio tracks: SRC (the assigned machine), LFO speed and depth, AMP, FX1 and FX2.
One scene: its locked values, wherever the crossfader is and even when that scene is muted.
The blend: the value stock's scene morph plays at the current crossfader position, rounded to the nearest knob step; a muted scene counts as not locked, exactly as stock morphs it.
On trigs: hold trigs in grid recording and press a scene key, or both: the scene's values, or the blend at the current fader position, become p-locks on those steps.
Nothing new is stored: the result is ordinary Part data that saves, loads and survives a power cycle like a hand-turned knob.
Pressing it when nothing would change shows NOTHING TO APPLY.
usage: Lock some parameters in SCENE A and SCENE B. Hold SCENE A (or SCENE B) and press YES to make that scene's values the Part's own: SCENE A APPLIED (or SCENE B APPLIED).
To keep an in-between sound, move the crossfader, hold SCENE A and SCENE B, and press YES: SCENE BLEND APPLIED.
Save the Part to keep it, or press FUNC + CUE (RELOAD PART) to go back to the last saved Part.
To put a scene on particular steps: in grid recording hold the trigs, press SCENE A (or SCENE B, or both for the blend) and let go: SCENE A TO TRIGS. Hold a trig and press PLAY to clear its p-locks.

limitations: YES with SCENE A, SCENE B or both held no longer shows ARM ALL; YES alone still does.

In grid recording, SCENE A or SCENE B pressed with trigs held writes p-locks when the last scene key is released. A trig pressed or a knob turned inside that gesture keeps its stock meaning (scene select, scene lock) and then nothing is written.

The crossfader stays where it is and the scenes keep their locks: a parameter locked in both scenes keeps its sound, while one locked in only one scene can change (after a one-scene apply it plays that lock at every fader position; after the blend stock blends that lock with the new base).
XVOL and XLV (the crossfader volume locks) have no Part knob and stay scene locks.
Trig locks and LFO modulation are not written into the Part; the result is the sound on steps without a trig lock.
On trigs: only the active track and the held steps of the trig page shown. There is no undo beyond stock's hold trig + PLAY, which clears all of that step's p-locks.
With MASTER TRACK on, track 8's SRC and AMP scene locks are not applied: stock has no knob there.
Not in MIDI mode, and not on MIDI tracks (stock has no scene locks there).
Undo is stock RELOAD PART, which also discards any other unsaved edits since the last Part save.

Tested on one MKII over USB: the Part apply with 0.1.0 (values watched, no audio check); TRIG + SCENE with 0.2.0, including playback by ear, a project save and a power cycle. Not tested on the MKI; the card build was not run on hardware.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: On a track playing a loop, hold SCENE A and turn FX1's first knob to the left; hold SCENE B and turn it to the right.

Hold SCENE A and press YES. SCENE A APPLIED appears, and FX1's first knob now shows scene A's value. Put the crossfader in the middle, hold SCENE A and SCENE B and press YES: SCENE BLEND APPLIED, and the knob shows the middle value.
